comment: Each public claim, where it is stated, and the evidence behind it. tests/test_claims_ledger.py fails if a claim's text disappears from its file, if a named test no longer exists, or if a banned phrase appears in the README or docs. 'verified' needs evidence; 'limitation' is something we say we do not do or know; an external claim lives outside this repository and is only listed.

claims.claim: Exactly four tools for an AI agent
None of them can approve, apply, stop or change a limit
approvals bound to
a stop that needs no approval
loopback by default
refuses DTDs and entities
These adapters are observe-only
Status: pre-alpha. Simulation only.
claims.note: Only simulated adapters are accepted by the Bridge; no hardware adapter exists.

claims.claim: If a workspace is set and the adapter cannot report positions, everything is refused
Nothing here controls real hardware
claims.note: An absence claim: backed by the Bridge refusing non-simulated adapters, not by a search of all code.

claims.claim: exact replay within one installed environment
claims.note: Within one environment only. See C11.

claims.claim: cross-machine repeatability is not claimed
claims.note: Not measured. A comparison across MuJoCo 3.17.0 and 4.0.0 is planned (issue 1130) and would still be two environments, not two machines.

claims.claim: not reviewed by native speakers
claims.note: Translations are AI-assisted drafts. Review calls: issues 1122, 1123 and 1281.

claims.claim: out-of-range
the AI can only adjust a tool offset
claims.note: The only command is set_tool_offset; the numbers in the machine-tool model are invented (see C15).

claims.claim: the wear-study numbers are invented
claims.note: External text (the project wiki), listed so that it is not forgotten.

claims.claim: 604 passed, 16 skipped (designed skips)
claims.where: wiki: Home.md and Roadmap.md, ragleap-physical rows

evidence.ref: Colab 2026-11-07, Python 3.13.18, pytest 8.4.2, MuJoCo 4.0.0, MCP SDK 1.30.0; run from the TestPyPI source archive of 0.0.5

claims.note: External text. The 16 skips are the control-only cases of four observe-only adapters, by design.

claims.claim: Not independently audited
claims.where: wiki: Home.md and Roadmap.md, ragleap-physical rows
claims.note: External text. The English README does not say it; the wiki does.

claims.claim: compared after Unicode NFKC normalisation and case folding
claims.note: Fixed in PR 1340 (issue 1337). Deliberate break checked: restoring the exact-text comparison fails the test. REAL, 2026-11-11, simulation only.

claims.claim: The stop flag is now checked again right before the first adapter call
claims.note: PR 1340 (issue 1339). Narrowed, not closed: see the next row. Deliberate break checked. REAL, 2026-11-11.

claims.claim: it does not close it for a stop from another thread that lands between the check and the call
claims.note: A full answer needs adapters to refuse commands while stopped. Issue 1339 stays open.

claims.claim: The one still open (#1338, a design question) is marked as an expected failure.
claims.note: An approval given before stop() can still be used after clear_stop(). The maintainer decides the design.

claims.claim: read and discard what the client still sends, for at most 0.5 s and 1 MiB
claims.note: PR 1341 (issue 1336). Checked on Linux only: five deliberate breaks caught. REAL, 2026-11-11. This row says nothing about Windows.

claims.claim: not verified on Windows
claims.note: Linux keeps the answer after the close, so it cannot show the symptom. A Windows retest of commit 99c47b1b or later is requested (issue 1114).

claims.claim: the console failure a Windows tester saw is not explained by it
claims.note: The console path drains small bodies, so the oversize-body cause does not explain it. Open.

claims.claim: The 0.0.3 refusal fix was not enough.
claims.note: A Windows tester still saw WinError 10053 on 0.0.3 and 0.0.5.
